To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) occupational cancers are a serious problem for Polish society and (2) there are several factors that can help to reduce the number of occupational cancers in Poland.
the incidence of cancer in the working population in Poland is lower in the group of employed people than in the general population.

(1) the incidence rate of all occupational cancer was 1.3 cases per 100,000 workers, with an annual average of 2,500 cases; (2) the incidence rate for lung cancer was 0.9 cases per 100 000 workers, with 1,600 annual cases; (3) the incidence rate per 100, 000 workers for mesothelioma was 0.2, and for bladder cancer 0.2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the occupational cancer incidence and mortality rates in Poland, and the assessment of their trends in 1995- 2003.
the identification of the occupational cancers in Poland.
the analysis of the incidence of occupational cancers in Poland, in the period from 1995-1999, 1995, 2000-2003, 2001-2003 and 2002-2003.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the occupational cancer burden in Poland is still high, and it is not declining.
the incidence of cancer in Poland has been rising in the last 20 years and that the incidence of the most common cancers has been stable.
the occupational cancer burden in Poland in the years 1995-1999 was estimated at 1 500-1 800 cases, and in the years 2000-2003 at 1 400-1 700 cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incidence of occupational cancer in Poland in the period 1995-2014 has decreased by 50%.
the incidence of occupational cancer in Poland is high and that there is a great need for improvement of the occupational health system.
in the period from 1995 to 2003 the incidence of cancers in the occupational environment has been stable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of people who are diagnosed with cancer each year is increasing.
